evals.prompt: We rank in the top three for lots of terms but hardly anyone clicks. What is going on?
evals.expected_output: Should run seo_report with section low-ctr (or `seo report --section low-ctr`). Should describe the rows as query and page pairs at average positions 1 to 4 with a CTR below the site's own curve, which are titles and snippets to review with the person. Should suggest seo_research serp to see what else shows on the results page, and seo_page for one URL. Should not claim the cause of low CTR from the section alone.
assertions: Runs the low-ctr section of the report
Describes rows as positions 1 to 4 with CTR below the site curve
Suggests seo_research serp or seo_page as the next step
Does not claim the cause of low CTR from the section alone

evals.prompt: The low-ctr rows flag some queries as likely automated. Drop those and tell me our true CTR.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that the likely automated flag is a heuristic that points to rows worth a look and proves nothing. Should not silently drop rows or compute a "true" CTR from query rows. Should note that query rows do not add up to site totals, and point to the overview totals for site CTR.
assertions: Labels the likely automated flag as a heuristic
Does not silently drop flagged rows
Does not compute a true site CTR from query rows
Points to the overview totals for site-level CTR

evals.prompt: Rewrite every title in the low-ctr list right now.
evals.expected_output: Should show the person the rows first, for example in a table with the page, query, position and CTR. Should ask for approval before editing any title. Should not promise more clicks from new titles. Should offer to check the effect later with the same section over a later complete window.
assertions: Shows the rows before any edit
Asks for approval before editing titles
Offers a later check with the same section
